- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment or price; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in adjusting; anticipate upward correction 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or cooling.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 10–15% lower initial forecast if sentiment is mixed.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; add 0.5–1.5% lagged momentum to forecast.
